# A Canadian company buys two US-listed shares in one transaction written
# wholly in US dollars.
#
# This is the book the carrying exists for. Nothing in that purchase states a
# Canadian figure: both holdings and the dollars that paid for them are in US
# dollars, so no split's value over its amount is the day's rate and a cost
# can be derived from nothing. What says what the shares cost is the cost basis
# the dollars came out of, at 1.30, and that rate travels onto what those
# dollars bought — apportioned by each split's own share of them.
#
# 2,200.00 USD leave a cost basis carrying 1.30, so 2,860.00 CAD of cost goes
# with them:
#
#     2,000.00 USD to USD_TECH  ->  2,600.00 CAD  ->  52.00 a share
#       200.00 USD to USD_CORP  ->    260.00 CAD  ->  26.00 a share
#
# Handing the whole 2,860.00 to the shares bought most of would price USD_TECH
# at 57.20 and leave USD_CORP at nothing.
#
# `tests/fixtures/a_broker_fee_two_us_loans_and_part_of_the_shares_sold.txt` is
# the same kind of trade with one split kept in Canadian dollars, and that one
# Canadian figure is enough for the cost to be derived from the transaction
# instead. The two books reach a cost by the two different routes, and only this
# one carries it.
#
# What happens:
#
# - 2029-01-02  15,000.00 CAD of opening capital.
# - 2029-01-05  10,000.00 USD bought at 1.30, so 13,000.00 CAD leaves the bank
#               and a cost basis of 10,000.00 USD at 1.30 opens.
# - 2029-01-08  50 USD_TECH at 40.00 USD and 10 USD_CORP at 20.00 USD, paid for
#               with 2,200.00 USD out of that cost basis. Stated wholly in US
#               dollars, which is how a US broker's confirmation reads.
# - 2029-12-30  20 USD_TECH sold at 55.00 USD. They cost 1,040.00 CAD — 20 at
#               52.00 — and fetch 1,100.00 USD at the 1.20 of the day, which is
#               1,320.00 CAD, so 280.00 CAD is realized.
#
# What is left at the year end: 30 USD_TECH costing 1,560.00 CAD, 10 USD_CORP
# costing 260.00 CAD, and 8,900.00 USD in the bank.
#
# Verified by
# tests/integration/test_a_share_purchase_stating_no_canadian_figure_is_costed_from_its_dollars.py.

	fraction: 100

	fraction: 10000

	mnemonic: "USD_CORP"
	fullname: "Another company whose shares are priced in US dollars"
	namespace: "NASDAQ"
	fraction: 10000

2029-01-05 * "Buy 10,000.00 USD at 1.30"
	currency.mnemonic: "CAD"
	Assets:USD Bank 10000.00 USD
		guid: "b2b2b2b2b2b2b2b2b2b2b2b2b2b20001"
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
		share_price: "13/10"
		value: "13000.00"
	Assets:CAD Bank -13000.00 CAD

# Every split is in US dollars, so nothing here says what a Canadian dollar is
# worth and no cost can be derived from the transaction. The 2,200.00 USD leave
# a cost basis carrying 1.30, and that rate travels onto both holdings, each
# taking its own share of it.
2029-01-08 * "Buy 50 USD_TECH at 40.00 USD and 10 USD_CORP at 20.00 USD"
	currency.mnemonic: "USD"
	Assets:Tech Shares 50.0000 USD_TECH
		guid: "b2b2b2b2b2b2b2b2b2b2b2b2b2b20002"
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "USD_TECH"
		share_price: "40"
		value: "2000.00"
	Assets:Corp Shares 10.0000 USD_CORP
		guid: "b2b2b2b2b2b2b2b2b2b2b2b2b2b20003"
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "USD_CORP"
		share_price: "20"
		value: "200.00"
	Assets:USD Bank -2200.00 USD
		cost_basis_split_guid: "b2b2b2b2b2b2b2b2b2b2b2b2b2b20001"

2029-12-30 * "Sell 20 USD_TECH at 55.00 USD"
	currency.mnemonic: "CAD"
	Assets:Tech Shares -20.0000 USD_TECH
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "USD_TECH"
		share_price: "52"
		value: "-1040.00"
		cost_basis_split_guid: "b2b2b2b2b2b2b2b2b2b2b2b2b2b20002"
	Assets:USD Bank 1100.00 USD
		guid: "b2b2b2b2b2b2b2b2b2b2b2b2b2b20004"
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
		share_price: "6/5"
		value: "1320.00"
	Income:Realized Gains $residual$ CAD
